clue.text: To avoid danger, eat only eggs now?

definitions.meaning: to rescue yourself from harm or trouble, in the idiom
a whimsical literal reading: keep the rashers back and breakfast on eggs alone

explanation.surface: Advice that the safe course is to stick to eggs at breakfast.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition takes the idiom literally: if you keep your bacon unused, eggs are all that is left on the plate.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to escape harm narrowly, so it fits avoiding danger.

clue.text: Caterer showing cook a short way

parts.note: to stew is to cook slowly
RD is the abbreviation for road, a way

explanation.surface: A caterer demonstrating a quick route.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward on a ship or plane provides food and drink to passengers.

clue.text: Ministers going round one university instead of another

indicators.note: going round says the clergymen surround the next pieces

parts.note: vicars are ministers of the church
I is the Roman numeral one
OU is the Open University

explanation.surface: Clergy taking the place of a university's own staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Something vicarious is done or felt on behalf of someone else.

clue.text: Ability to express nothing risque

parts.note: O, the zero shape, means nothing
racy means risque, slightly indecent

explanation.surface: Being able to talk without saying anything rude.
explanation.definitionFit: Oracy is skill in speaking, the spoken counterpart of literacy.

clue.text: Prominence of ecstasy and speed in current circumstances

parts.note: E is slang for the drug ecstasy
mph, miles per hour, measures speed
as is means in the present state, as things stand

explanation.surface: Drug use featuring heavily in today's world.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphasis is special importance or prominence given to something.

clue.text: Cook sounds like an ass, we hear

indicators.note: we hear asks for the sound of the word rather than its spelling

parts.note: a donkey makes the noise called braying, so it brays

explanation.surface: A chef with a voice like a donkey.
explanation.definitionFit: To braise is to cook slowly in a little liquid in a closed pot.

clue.text: Initially causing a stir about a cover for horse

indicators.note: Initially picks out the opening letter of causing
about says the prison word goes around the second a

parts.note: stir is slang for prison

explanation.surface: A horse blanket that causes a sensation.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth draped over a horse.

clue.text: What's in this bottle? Never rum

indicators.note: rum, meaning odd, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bottle labelled as containing anything but rum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bottle' is British slang for courage, so the bottle holds courage, not a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve means courage, which British slang also calls bottle.

clue.text: Bachelor, lissom and light-hearted

parts.note: B is the abbreviation for bachelor, as in BA
lissom and lithe both mean supple

explanation.surface: Describing a carefree, supple young single man.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithe means cheerful and carefree.

clue.text: Briefly held what Cleopatra fatally grasped in embrace

parts.note: encl. is the short form of enclosed, meaning held within
Cleopatra is said to have died by clasping a venomous snake, an asp, to her breast

explanation.surface: An account of Cleopatra's death, clutching the snake to her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Briefly' marks an abbreviation: ENCL, as written on letters, stands for enclosed.
explanation.definitionFit: To clasp something in your arms is to hug or embrace it.

clue.text: In dismay about costume

indicators.note: placed first, In says the word for 'about' goes inside the word for dismay

parts.note: to dismay someone is to appal them
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: Someone horrified by an outfit.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is clothing, and a costume is a set of clothes.

clue.text: Australian river backing up produces impressive display

indicators.note: backing up in a down-the-page sense tells us the river's name runs backwards

parts.note: the Yarra is the river that flows through Melbourne

explanation.surface: A river in Australia surging back over its banks is a sight to see.
explanation.definitionFit: An array is an imposing arrangement or show of things.

clue.text: Taking in sailors and soldiers with talent

parts.note: an AB is an able seaman, so ABs are sailors
OR stands for Other Ranks, ordinary soldiers
a bent is a natural talent or aptitude

explanation.surface: Recruiting from the navy and army, picking those with ability.
explanation.definitionFit: Something absorbent soaks up liquid, that is, takes it in.

clue.text: Proverbially lifeless stud

definitions.meaning: the saying 'dead as a ...' names this object as the type of deadness
a large-headed nail once used to stud doors

explanation.definitionFit: The proverb 'dead as a doornail' makes it a byword for lifelessness, and it is also a stud-like nail.

clue.text: Shape of Western woodland

indicators.note: Shape says the letters are moulded into a new form

explanation.surface: The outline of some forest in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEW FOREST is an ancient woodland in Hampshire, southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The New Forest is a large area of ancient forest and heath in Hampshire.

clue.text: Temporary relief from wild plant? Not always

definitions.meaning: a getaway or break from everyday cares
a garden plant that has gone feral is found growing wild, though it was not always so

explanation.walkthrough: Botanists call a cultivated plant now growing wild an escape: it was once tame, hence 'Not always'.
explanation.definitionFit: An escape is a break from routine, and in botany a cultivated plant gone wild.

clue.text: Granting access

definitions.meaning: entry, as to a building or event

explanation.definitionFit: An admission is both a concession that something is true and permission to enter.

clue.text: Wave foreign money in error

indicators.note: in says the currency sits inside the word for error

parts.note: bish is British slang for a mistake
the rand is the currency of South Africa

explanation.surface: Waving about foreign currency by mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: BISH is dated British slang for a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: To brandish something is to wave it about.

clue.text: Deny outside is blue

indicators.note: outside puts the word for blue around the little word is

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling down

explanation.surface: Someone refuses to admit to being sad.
explanation.definitionFit: To disown something is to refuse to acknowledge it, to deny it.

clue.text: Deliver verdict, clearing one from unholy crime

indicators.note: clearing means getting rid of, so a letter is taken away

parts.note: deicide, killing a god, is the most unholy crime
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A judge acquits one defendant of an unholy offence.
explanation.definitionFit: To decide is to settle a matter, as a court does in giving a verdict.

clue.text: Broadcast route covers motorway

indicators.note: covers says the word for route wraps around the motorway letter

parts.note: a transit is a passage or route
M is the abbreviation for motorway, as in the M1

explanation.surface: A radio report on traffic along a motorway.
explanation.definitionFit: To broadcast a programme is to send it out on air.

clue.text: Gymnastic equipment teacher's beginning to demolish outside gym lesson

indicators.note: beginning picks out the first letter of teacher's
outside says the demolition word goes around the gym lesson

parts.note: to raze is to demolish completely
PE, physical education, is a school gym lesson

explanation.surface: A teacher wrecks equipment outside a gym class.
explanation.definitionFit: A trapeze is a swinging bar used by gymnasts and acrobats.

clue.text: Hog a lot of time available for business

parts.note: a hog is a pig
an eon is an immensely long time

explanation.surface: A greedy person monopolising time free for work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not my pigeon' means not my concern, so the bird stands for one's business.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's pigeon is their concern or affair, as in 'not my pigeon'.

clue.text: Person keeping a discount in error

indicators.note: in error says the letters are mistakenly placed and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper who wrongly gave a discount.
explanation.definitionFit: A custodian is a guardian or keeper of something.

clue.text: Hammock used aboard ship from Glasgow, perhaps

indicators.note: aboard says the bed goes inside the ship letters

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a cot is a hanging bed on board ship

explanation.surface: A sailor's hammock from a Glasgow vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is in Scotland, so people from there are Scots.

clue.text: Dough essential to keep a stable

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Money is vital to running a horse stable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dough' suggests money in the surface; here it is literal dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Pasta is made from a flour-and-egg paste, a kind of dough.

clue.text: Academic concealing old evidence

indicators.note: concealing says the academic hides the letter for old inside

parts.note: prof is short for professor

explanation.surface: A professor hiding evidence.
explanation.definitionFit: Proof is evidence that establishes a fact.

clue.text: Ice does, when it re-forms — see!

indicators.note: re-forms says the letters are shaped again into a new word

explanation.surface: Ice melting and freezing again is presented as a marvel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a bishop's see, not an instruction to look.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's see is the district under his authority.

clue.text: To show veneration to girl is prostrate when speaking

indicators.note: when speaking says we want the sound of the phrase, not its spelling

parts.note: Ida, a girl's name, plus lies, being prostrate

explanation.surface: Worshipping a girl who lies face down.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic accent 'Ida lies' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To idolise someone is to revere or worship them.

clue.text: Hold official enquiry into boundary hedge

parts.note: a tribunal sits on a case it is investigating
the fence is the boundary of a field or garden

explanation.surface: An inquiry is held into a disputed garden hedge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hedge' looks like part of the boundary; it is the verb, to avoid committing.
explanation.definitionFit: To hedge is to avoid taking a side, which is what this idiom describes.
